body:
### Summary


## Summary

`uv lock --locked`, `uv lock --check`, `uv sync --locked` and `uv sync --check` all
report a lockfile as up-to-date even though the **locked resolution does not
satisfy the project's declared dependency specifiers** — as long as the lockfile's
recorded *declarations* (the root package's `[package.metadata] requires-dist`)
match `pyproject.toml`.

This makes it trivial to produce a lockfile that passes every CI guard
(`uv sync --locked`) while quietly installing different package versions than
`pyproject.toml` declares. We hit this in production: a hand-edited `uv.lock`
declared `kifv-model-serving==2.3.0rc2` but resolved `2.2.7`; every check passed
and our deployed images silently ran the old version.

I understand the design constraint (registry sources are `is_immutable()`, so
`Lock::satisfies` deliberately skips them to avoid metadata refreshes), but I
believe a cheap check is missing: **the locked version on each dependency edge
from a workspace member is already known statically and can be validated against
the declared specifier with a pure PEP 440 `contains()` test — no network, no
metadata fetch.**

## Environment

- uv 0.12.3 (507230998 2026-08-07 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)
- CPython 3.13.15
- Reproduces against public PyPI (no custom indexes needed)

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
uv init --no-workspace demo && cd demo
cat > pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
[project]
name = "demo"
version = "0.0.1"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["six==1.16.0"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.uv]
package = false
EOF

uv lock   # resolves six==1.16.0, requires-dist = [{ name = "six", specifier = "==1.16.0" }]

# "Hand-edit" the lockfile the way a confused human/tool would:
# bump the declaration to match pyproject, but leave the resolution stale.
sed -i 's/six==1.16.0/six==1.17.0/' pyproject.toml
sed -i 's/{ name = "six", specifier = "==1.16.0" }/{ name = "six", specifier = "==1.17.0" }/' uv.lock

# The lockfile now says:
#   pyproject:          six==1.17.0
#   [requires-dist]:    six==1.17.0   (declaration — bumped)
#   [[package]] six:    1.16.0        (resolution  — stale, still valid/self-consistent:
#                                      1.16.0 wheels + hashes present)

uv lock --locked   # exit 0 ❌  "Resolved 2 packages" — accepted
uv lock --check    # exit 0 ❌  accepted
uv sync --locked   # exit 0 ❌  installs six==1.16.0 against the declared ==1.17.0
uv sync --check    # exit 0 ❌  "Found up-to-date lockfile" / "Would make no changes"
uv pip list        # six     1.16.0   ← despite pyproject requiring ==1.17.0
```

Control case (works correctly today): if `uv.lock` is *not* hand-edited — i.e.
only `pyproject.toml` changes — all of the above correctly fail with
"The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--locked` was provided."

## Actual behavior

All four commands exit 0. `uv sync` installs the stale locked version
(`six==1.16.0`) although the project declares `six==1.17.0`. The inconsistency
between the recorded declaration and the recorded resolution is never detected,
not even by the lockfile parser (which validates other static invariants, e.g.
wheel-filename/version consistency via `InconsistentVersions`).

## Expected behavior

At least one of:

1. `Lock::satisfies` (or the lockfile deserializer) validates that each locked
   dependency version satisfies the specifier recorded on the dependency
   declaration. Both sides are already in the lockfile (or in
   `pyproject.toml` during the same validation run); this is a PEP 440
   `VersionSpecifiers::contains(locked_version)` check on the root's edges —
   no network, no metadata refresh, no conflict with the `is_immutable()`
   fast path. A failure would surface as e.g.
   `SatisfiesResult::MismatchedRequirements`, so `--locked`/`--check` would
   exit non-zero, exactly as they already do for the control case above.
2. Arguably the lockfile parser should reject such a file outright
   (`package.metadata.requires_dist` says `==1.17.0` while the edge resolves
   `six (1.16.0)`), similar to the existing malformed-wheel check.

## Notes

- Same class of hole for transitive deps: a hand-edited `[[package]]` version
  with matching (hand-edited or stale) wheel entries is accepted because
  registry packages are skipped in validation. Validating edge specifiers from
  mutable (workspace) packages would at least close the direct-dependency case,
  which is where pins live.
- Root cause pointer (uv 0.12.3, `crates/uv-resolver/src/lock/mod.rs`):
  `Lock::satisfies` → declarations are compared
  (`MismatchedRequirements` / `MismatchedPackageRequirements`), then the walk
  does `if package.id.source.is_immutable() { continue; }`, and `is_immutable()`
  is true for `Source::Registry(..)`. Nothing anywhere compares a locked
  registry version against the declared version specifiers.
- `--check` is an alias of `--locked` for both `uv lock` and `uv sync`, so all
  spellings share the gap.

### Platform

any

### Version

uv 0.13.7 (316c827e0 2026-11-03 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

_No response_
title: `--locked`/`--check` accept a lockfile whose resolution violates the declared specifiers (declaration-only validation)
